Problem: Higher batching can reduce cost but increase consumer delivery duration.
RootCauseHypothesis: Optimizing a local operational objective can worsen another stakeholder outcome; joint optimization is required.
EvidenceSummary: DoorDash engineering explicitly describes the batch-rate tradeoff between Dasher cost and consumer delivery duration.
InternalValidation: Estimate marginal effects of batch rate by supply state on delivery duration, cost, merchant wait and cancellation.
RecommendedControl: Joint multi-objective optimization with explicit guardrails.
SuccessKPI: Cost per delivery; delivery duration; cancellation; merchant wait; batch rate.

Problem: Supply incentives and assignment decisions can interact.
RootCauseHypothesis: Separate decision systems can each be locally rational but jointly suboptimal.
EvidenceSummary: DoorDash describes jointly optimizing supply mobilization and assignment/batch decisions rather than treating them independently.
InternalValidation: Replay the same market states under separate vs joint policies and measure total-cost/quality outcomes.
RecommendedControl: Shared objective function and joint optimization / policy coordination.
SuccessKPI: Total cost subject to delivery-quality constraints.

Problem: NYC settlement addressed underpayment and missed/delayed payments.
RootCauseHypothesis: Technical issues and complex delivery scenarios can create compensation errors when event state, jurisdiction and rule logic interact.
EvidenceSummary: Reuters reports a $131.5M settlement; DoorDash cited technical issues and complex scenarios including cross-boundary complications and said the problems were fixed.
InternalValidation: Reconstruct event timelines by trip/order with jurisdiction, online/active time, batch/cancellation state, rule version, expected pay, actual pay and payout status.
RecommendedControl: Event-level pay ledger with versioned rules and expected-vs-actual reconciliation before payout closure.
SuccessKPI: Pay variance; late payout; unresolved payout exceptions; rule-test coverage.

Problem: Dasher compensation and pay models are a continuing regulatory risk area.
RootCauseHypothesis: Location-specific rules increase rule-management and regression-test complexity.
EvidenceSummary: DoorDash 10-Q discusses investigations and inquiries involving Dasher classification, compensation, pay models and pay practices.
InternalValidation: Map each pay decision to jurisdiction, rule version, effective date and eligible population; monitor exceptions by market.
RecommendedControl: Central rule catalog, effective-dating, jurisdiction tests and auditability.
SuccessKPI: Jurisdiction mismatch; rule coverage; compliance exception aging.
